summary: PETG corner shelf plate that replaces a glass corner shelf in two existing wall brackets (one on each wall of a 90 deg corner, far edge of each bracket 152.4 mm / 6 in from the corner). Mostly square: 170 x 170, two edges along the walls. Only the front corner (opposite the wall corner) gets a subtle R40 curve; the other three corners are rounded R4. R1.2 top edge roundover, 0.4 bottom elephant-foot chamfer. 7.8 mm thick so it drops into the brackets like the 7.9 mm glass. Printed flat on a Bambu Lab A1 mini (180 x 180), 5 mm margin.

assumptions: A1: the wall corner is 90 deg and both brackets are at the same height and the same distance from the corner (input/20261107_143349.jpg). A wall 1 deg off square moves a tip about 3 mm, which the brackets absorb.
A2: the brackets clamp the plate edge with their screws, as with the glass; the plate needs no holes or tabs.
A3: the plate is the same shape on both walls (symmetric about the diagonal).

A4 (rev 2): the plate carries load but should not be a solid block (user: 'you decide what should be the best fill with min material use, 282 is too much I need stuctural streghtn rather than make a block'). Sandwich print: 4 walls, 6/6 top/bottom layers (1.2 mm skins), 20 % gyroid core. About 104 cm3, 130 g (100 % would be 282 g).
A5: plate thickness 7.8 (39 layers) rather than 7.9 so it is never thicker than the old glass; if it rattles, the clamp screws are tightened a little more.
A6: PETG is used because the shelf sits in a wet shower area (PETG takes water and up to about 70 deg C).
A7: the shelf face is flat like the glass; no drain holes or lip.
